title: The glide /j/
goal: Practise /j/ and use it in a short, understandable exchange.
cue: Raise the front of the tongue close to the roof of the mouth, then move into the next vowel. The phonetic symbol /j/ is the sound at the start of yes, not the letter name J.
spelling: y at the beginning of yes represents /j/. The letter y has other sounds in other positions.
task: Ask permission to sit. Reply with a clear yes or no.
story: A yellow cup is by you. You can use it.
reviewPrompt: Return to day 14, 21, 25, 27. Recall a word or say one useful phrase before opening those lessons.

articulation.label: yet
articulation.alt: yet: /j/ → /ɛ/ → /t/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /j/: Front tongue high; glide into the next vowel.
/ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/t/: Tongue tip touches the ridge, then releases.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
